media_groups.description:
This visualization shows Sea Surface Temperature (SST) Anomaly data from the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) Multi-scale Ultra-high Resolution (MUR) Sea Surface Temperature Analysis. The analysis data is near-real-time (one day latency) and the visualization is updated daily to include the latest available data.

Data available here: https://podaac.jpl.nasa.gov/dataset/MUR-JPL-L4-GLOB-v4.1

related.title: El Niño 2026: Sea Surface Temperature Anomaly (2025 vs. 2026) – Updated Daily
related.description: A side-by-side comparison of sea surface temperature anomalies in the tropical Pacific during 2025 and 2026, highlighting ocean temperature patterns associated with El Niño. This visualization is updated daily to incorporate the latest available data.

main_image.alt_text: Two side-by-side globes centered on the tropical Pacific Ocean, comparing sea surface temperature anomalies in 2025 and 2026. Red and blue shading highlights warmer- and cooler-than-average ocean temperatures, with a color bar legend showing the temperature differences in degrees Celsius.

related.title: Sea Surface Height Anomaly (SSHA) - Updated weekly
related.description: A series of Sea Surface Height Anomaly (SSHA) visualizations in several projections, automatically updated each week.

main_image.alt_text: A global map in an Atlantic-centered rectangular projection showing the most recent available sea surface height anomaly data. Ocean colors range from dark blue through light blue and white to yellow and red, revealing geographic patterns of lower- and higher-than-average sea surface heights. Contour lines, date labels, and a color legend are included.

products.title: Signs of El Niño in 2026
products.description: These visualizations compare ocean conditions in the tropical Pacific during the same months in 2025 and 2026, using sea surface temperature, ocean color, and sea surface height data. Together, they highlight changes in the ocean that may signal the development of El Niño conditions.

main_image.alt_text: Six animated maps of the tropical Pacific Ocean arranged in two columns and three rows compare ocean conditions in 2025 and 2026. The top row shows sea surface temperature anomalies, the middle row shows apparent visible wavelength, and the bottom row shows sea surface height anomalies. Color changes highlight differences between the two years, with labels identifying potential signals of El Niño in 2026.
